A.explanation: Gives about one-tenth of the required $D$, consistent with a power-of-ten error when converting $650 \text{ nm}$, $0.12 \text{ mm}$ and $7.5 \text{ cm}$ to metres.

B.explanation: Gives about one-fifth of the required $D$, consistent with an error in rearranging $x = \lambda D / a$ or in handling the small slit separation.

C.explanation: Gives about half the required $D$, consistent with doubling $a$ or halving $x$ in the calculation.

D.explanation: Using $D = ax/\lambda$ with SI values gives about $14 \text{ m}$, matching the large fringe spacing from the small slit separation.

hints: Notice the three lengths in different units: wavelength $650 \text{ nm}$, slit separation $0.12 \text{ mm}$ and fringe separation $7.5 \text{ cm}$ - all must be in metres before use.
Recall how double-slit fringe spacing $x$ depends on wavelength $\lambda$, slit separation $a$ and screen distance $D$: larger $D$ or $\lambda$ widens fringes, larger $a$ narrows them.
Rearrange to $D = ax/\lambda$, then substitute $a = 1.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$, $x = 0.075 \text{ m}$ and $\lambda = 650 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$ and check the metre result.
walkthrough: Convert all lengths to SI units: $\lambda = 650 \text{ nm} = 650 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$, $a = 0.12 \text{ mm} = 1.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$, and fringe spacing $x = 7.5 \text{ cm} = 0.075 \text{ m}$.
State the two-slit interference rule for bright fringe separation: $x = \lambda D / a$, where $D$ is the slits-to-screen distance.
Rearrange for the unknown distance: $D = ax/\lambda$.
Substitute with units: $D = (1.2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m})(0.075 \text{ m}) / (650 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m})$.
Calculate the numerator: $(1.2 \times 10^{-4})(0.075) = 9.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$, then $D = 9.0 \times 10^{-6} / 650 \times 10^{-9} \approx 13.8 \text{ m}$.
Round sensibly to about $14 \text{ m}$ with unit $\text{m}$. This is option D.
